1.x: A Trinitarian sees God-the-Spirit leading God-the-Son into the wilderness while God-the-Father is up in heaven. A Oneness Christian sees the one true God who is Spirit (Jn 4:24; 17:3) leading His human Son into the wilderness. As Israel was “led” into the wilderness by YHWH(Deut 8:2-5), so was the man Jesus (as the New Israel) “led” into the wilderness by the same YHWH. The Spirit, which was also involved in the conception of the Son because it’s literally the Father of the man Jesus (Mt 1:20), initiated the Son’s testing. The human Son is the one being tested, since God (the divine Spirit) cannot be tempted by evil (Jms 1:13). Christ (the human) was tempted in all points (Heb 4:15; 1 Jn 2:16); Satan tempted him with “the lust of the flesh” (Mt 4:2-3), “the lust of the eyes” (v 8-9), and “the pride of life” (v 5-6).

For a Trinitarian the Son is also God, so they would say that only his “human nature” is tempted, not his “divine nature.” But how can one person have two wills & two natures that contradict each other (human vs divine)? Does Jesus know all things, or does he not know all things (Mk 13:32)? Is he eternal or does he die (1 Cor 15:3)? Is Jesus omniscient or did he have to grow in wisdom (Lk 2:52)? If you say that Jesus simply “veiled” his “divine nature” or “emptied himself”, then, did he cease to be God since he didn’t have the divine attributes of omnipresence, omniscience and omnipotence anymore? How can anyone be “God” without those divine attributes? And once “veiled,” how does he have the ability to bring back his powers? Did he just pretend to “veil” his powers but he always had access to them? Does that mean he never truly lived like an authentic human being? These are problems only Trinitarians have because Oneness know that the one true God is Spirit (Jn 4:24), which fully dwelt in His human Son (Col 2:9-10) and glorifies the human (Jn 8:54 BSB) as His eternal visible image (Col 1:15; Rev 22:3-4). Oneness Christians don’t have any issues accepting that the human is useless without the divine Spirit: “I can of mine own self do nothing” (Jn 5:30 KJV) & “The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do” (Jn 5:19 KJV). This is because the Father is the one true God: “And this is life eternal, that they might know thee (1) the only true God, and (2) Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent” (Jn 17:3 KJV) & “For there is one (“heis”: singular masculine one) God, and one mediator between God and men, the MAN(not another god) Christ Jesus” (1 Tim 2:5 KJV). The Son is the perfect instrument of redemption for the Father: “God(the Father) was IN Christ, reconciling the world unto HIMSELF” (2 Cor 5:19 KJV). The Son is the human character that God chose in order to enter into our limited time & space. Think of it like a human playing video games and choosing a character to play with in the virtual world. The one God came to us from His Spiritual realm into our dimension through the human Jesus in order to let us know of the Spiritual world beyond our perceived reality: “I and my Father are one(“hen”: neuter form of one)” (Jn 10:30 KJV) - notice the lack of a Trinity, rather you see: “(1) “I”: an authentic human Jesus & (2) “my Father”: the one true God who is an invisible Spirit.

2.x: Matthew continues to push the idea of Jesus as the New Israel. Here, he explains how Jesus fasted for 40 days in the wilderness corresponding to the 40 years of testing in the wilderness by Israel (Deut 8:2-3). When God’s son (Israel) failed (Hos 11:1), Jesus (literally God’s Son) succeeded. Forty days is about the longest a human can fast without permanent bodily harm. Moses also fasted for forty days (Deut 9:9) and Elijah (1 Kings 19:8).

God Himself says: “PRAY UNTO ME” (Jer 29:12 KJV), “CALL UPON ME in the day of trouble” (Ps 50:15 KJV), “I will HEAR” (Isa 65:24 KJV), “let your requests BE MADE KNOWN UNTO GOD” (Phil 4:6 KJV), etc. Jesus Himself said: “After this manner therefore pray ye: Our FATHER..’” (Mt 6:9 KJV). Check study notes for “Matthew 6:5-6,” “Matthew 6:9,” “Matthew 6:10” and (coming soon) “Rev 5:8” for a more detailed explanation. “Dulia” comes from the Greek “douleia”, which simply means “slavery”, “serving as a slave,” or “bondservice”. “Slave” is “doulos”, so doing “Dulia” means you serve as a slave. “Hyperdulia” means hyper-slave-like-service. 11.x: Unlike Israel in the OT, this New Israel actually defeated Satan.

12.x: John had been arrested for his bold rebuke of Herod Antipas (Mt 14:3-4). Herod Antipas was Herod the Great’s son who was placed in charge of the Galilean area.

13.x: Capernaum is on the northern shore of the Sea of Galilee. This will remain Jesus’ base of operations and his new hometown for the duration of his ministry in Galilee. Capernaum was the home of Peter & Andrew (Mt 4:18), James & John (v 21), and Matthew (Mt 9:9). His move was strategic; he moved from Nazareth (a secluded, inland hill town), to Capernaum (one of the most important trade routes of the ancient world). This fulfills a prophecy from Isaiah 9:1-2. Zebulun and Naphtali are two of the original 12 Tribes of Israel. Zebulun is the 10th son of Jacob (the sixth of Leah), and Nephtali was the sixth son of Jacob (the second of Bilhah, Rachel’s handmaid). When tribes were allocated land in Joshua 19, Zebulun and Naphtali were given the northernmost regions, surrounding the Sea of Galilee. Because of their location on the northern border, these two tribes were the “front line” for every invasion from the north (Assyria, Babylon, etc). They were the first to be attacked and the first to be taken into exile. By the time of Jesus, this area was known as “Galilee of the Gentiles” because it was seen as spiritually “compromised” and physically war-torn. Matthew quotes a prophecy from 700 years earlier to show that God hadn’t forgotten these “marginalized” branches. Jesus began preaching in the “broken” border tribes of Zebulun & Naphtali first. He is looking for the place where his light is needed most. By making Capernaum (in the territory of Naphtali) his home, Jesus was saying that the True Vine grows best where people realize they cannot survive without the sap.

17.x: This marks the beginning of Jesus’ public ministry in Galilee. Immediately after getting baptized, Jesus is then led to the wilderness for 40 days. If you only read Matthew, it seems like Jesus withdraws into Galilee straight from the temptation. However, John 1-4 reveals that Jesus had an entire phase of ministry in Judea and Samaria first. He met Andrew, Peter, and Nathanael shortly after the wilderness. He does the first miracle at the wedding of Cana (Jn 2:11). He cleanses the temple in his first trip to Jerusalem for Passover (Jn 2:15-16), and he encounters the Samaritan woman at the well (Jn 4:7). The trigger point in Galilee was John’s arrest. John the Baptist was the “forerunner”, as long as John was preaching, Jesus remained somewhat in the background. If his baptism was on day 0, Jesus began preaching in Galilee at about 1 year after. Chronology: (1) “Jesus’ Baptism” (Mt 3:13-17); (2) “Jesus tempted in the wilderness” (Mt 4:1-11); (3) “Jesus at the wedding of Cana & the Samaritan woman” (Jn 1-4); (4) “Jesus begins preaching in Galilee” (Mt 4:17).

This is where the Pharisees & Sadducees loved to be seen by men. Satan is suggesting that Jesus launch his ministry not through the long, difficult path set by the Father, but through spectacular “stunts” that would bring him the praise of men. “For it is written”: Satan can use Scripture to tempt people. The best lies have a lot of truth in them. Discernment is not being able to tell between right & wrong; discernment is being able to tell between right & almost-right. Not everyone who claims to speak for God is true. Christianity is having faith in the Word of God, as given in Scripture. Notice how Jesus replied with MORE SCRIPTURE, without taking it out of context like Satan had done. 8-10.x: Jesus knew that he was destined to rule the kingdoms of the world (Rev 11:15). However, the “Father’s path” to that throne required the Cross, the Emptying, and the Death. Satan was offering a “painless” shortcut, a “throne without the thorns.” The pain we feel has its purpose, Jesus needed to go through that path to fulfill the Father’s Will and to prepare him to judge us fairly (Jn 5:22), fully understanding what it’s like to be human: “For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin” (Heb 4:15 KJV). “Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God … For in that he himself hath suffered being tempted, he is able to succour them that are tempted“(Heb 2:17-18 KJV). Jesus had to experience the full range of emotions and temptations (including stress, sorrow, fear, anger, exhaustion, etc) so He can truly empathize with us, not theoretically, but from personal experience. He felt sadness “even unto death” (Mt 26:38 KJV). He experienced stress to the point of sweating blood (Lk 22:44). “Jesus wept” (Jn 11:35 KJV), felt anger at the temple with the money changers (Jn 2:15), felt joy (Lk 10:21), felt exhaustion/weariness (Jn 4:6), needed rest (Mk 6:31), was despised of the people (Isa 53:3), etc. He demonstrated that it was possible to triumph over physical & emotional pain. Once we understand that pain is part of life, we can live in the peace that God gives us. The pain God puts us through has a purpose, it develops the character & faith that God needs for His kingdom.

21-22.x: The NT mentions several men named James (Jacob in Hebrew). To avoid confusion, it is important to notice how people are identified in the Gospels. Most individuals are distinguished by their father or their hometown. For example: “James son of Zebedee”; “James son of Alphaeus”; “Mary of Magdala” (Mary Magdalene). However, Jesus’ own family members are almost always identified in relation to Jesus himself. Examples include: “the mother OF JESUS” (Jn 2:1 KJV); “Mary HIS mother” (Mt 2:11 KJV); “HIS brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas” (Mt 13:55 KJV); “James THE LORD’S brother” (Gal 1:19 KJV). This pattern is significant in the discussion about whether Mary had other children after Jesus. In the Gospels, we encounter three main individuals named James: (1) James son of Zebedee (also called James the Greater): He was one of the twelve apostles and part of Jesus’ inner circle along with Peter and his brother John. He witnessed the Transfiguration, the raising of Jairus’ daughter, and Jesus’ agony in Gethsemane. He was the first apostle to be martyred (Acts 12:2). (2) James son of Alphaeus (also called James the Less or James the Younger): He was also one of the twelve apostles. He is usually distinguished as “the Less” or “the Younger,” probably because he was either shorter or younger than James, son of Zebedee. His mother is mentioned several times as “Mary the mother of James the Less” (Mk 15:40 KJV), “Mary the mother of James and Joses” (Mt 27:56 KJV), and simply “the other Mary” (Mt 27:61 KJV). Catholics try to argue that this James is the same person as “James the Lord’s brother,” making him a cousin or close relative rather than a biological brother of Jesus. (3) James, the brother of Jesus (traditionally called James the Just): He is the James mentioned in Mt 13:55 & Gal 1:19. During Jesus’ earthly ministry, he was not yet a believer (John 7:5), hence DIFFERENTIATED FROM THE TWO JAMES THAT ARE APOSTLES (believers). After the resurrection, he became a leader of the Jerusalem church and is traditionally considered the author of the Epistle of James. Even extra biblical history supports the fact that this James is an actual biological brother of Jesus: “the brother of Jesus, who was called Christ, whose name was James…” (Josephus in Antiquities of the Jews 20.9.1, ~93AC). The distinction between these James’ is important. James the brother of Jesus is consistently identified in relation to Jesus (“the Lord’s brother”), whereas James the Less is consistently identified through his mother (“Mary the mother of James the Less”), not in relation to Jesus. This difference in identification, along with the word “until” in Matthew 1:25 strongly suggests that Mary WAS NOT a perpetual virgin, but only “until” Jesus was born.

23-25.x: The gospel had gone beyond Jewish territory. It spread to Syria & Decapolis (Gentile territory). By starting his ministry in a border region like Capernaum, Jesus was positioned perfectly to reach the Gentiles. These verses also show Jesus’ three-fold ministry: (1) teaching; (2) preaching; (3) healing. “Teaching in their synagogues”: synagogues were born out of necessity, not from a direct command from God. In 586BC, the Babylonians destroyed the Temple and exiled the Jews. The Israelites needed a way to stay connected while in a foreign land, so they began to meet in homes to study the Scriptures and pray. By the time the Jews returned to Israel, the “synagogue” (Greek for “assembly” or “bringing together”) had become a permanent fixture in every town. And even though God didn’t ordain them, Jesus accepted them and used them as his primary “headquarters” for teaching. The history of the synagogue provides a powerful validation for why we have different denominations and worship styles today. It shows that while the Truth (the Vine) is eternal and unchanging, the Tradition (the trellis the vine grows on) often adapts to the needs of the people. However, while Jesus accepted the synagogue, he fiercely corrected the Pharisees when they turned their tradition into man-made commandments that actually kept people away from God’s real commandments: “Howbeit in vain do they worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men. For laying aside the commandment of God, ye hold the tradition of men” (Mk 7:7-8 KJV).
